articles.title: Farewell, Dr Frank-N-Furter: why Tim Curry’s Rocky Horror Show will go on
articles.summary: The versatile stage performer will always be remembered for his defining film role in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, which turned him into an icon of 70s underground cinema and proto-punk • Tim Curry, star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show and Stephen King’s It, dies aged 80 • Tim Curry on…
body: Over the past decade, the issues of trans identity and gender fluidity couldn’t have been more contemporary, and Tim Curry was an integral part of what might be called their pre-history in pop culture. He was an icon – though maybe now a dimly remembered icon – of the 70s underground cinema and proto-punk.

Curry was a good-looking actor with a tremendous speaking and singing voice, and a versatile performer – he got Tony nominations for his varied stage work on Broadway as Salieri in Amadeus, Alan Swann in My Favorite Year (the part Peter O’Toole played on screen) and as King Arthur in Monty Python’s Spamalot. But it was his strange destiny to be remembered for one role: at once indelibly prominent and weirdly peripheral. He was the sensational Dr Frank-N-Furter in the thoroughly outrageous Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975), the screen version of the 1973 stage show.

articles.title: My First Interview With Dolly Parton: Coming Face to Face With the Country Queen Who Soundtracked My Life
articles.summary: I am sitting on a couch in a hotel suite in midtown Manhattan. I have two tape recorders on the coffee table ready to document my interview with one of my idols. I hear someone whistling from behind French doors. It’s not just any person whose whistle I hear. It’s Dolly Parton and she is
body: There she is – Dolly Parton. She’s wearing a pink cashmere sweater and a pink tweed miniskirt. Her heels are high as her hair.

I stand up and extend my hand. But Parton apparently isn’t a handshake kind of gal. She leans in for a hug. She smells like candy. As we separate, I let out a small breath. Parton looks at me and smiles, letting me know that I have nothing to be nervous about. I smile back and we settle into the couch, sitting side-by-side and chatting for the next hour or so.
It was 2001. I was there to interview Parton for US Weekly for the launch of her 37 th studio album and the second of her three bluegrass albums, “Little Sparrow.”
It would be the first of many interviews I had with Parton over the next couple of decades.

articles.title: Telluride’s Julie Huntsinger on Her 20 Years Leading the Festival, Chasing ‘Digger’ and ‘Dune 3’ and a ‘True TBA’ Film Hidden Until Patrons Walk Into the Theater
articles.summary: Julie Huntsinger has spent two decades as the guardian of the Telluride Film Festival — a jewel box of off-duty movie stars and power players relaxing in the mountains and a consequential launchpad for the fall awards season. As festival director, Huntsinger has her hallmarks.
body: Huntsinger sits down with Variety to discuss secret negotiations, the ones that got away and why she calls herself a “midwife.”

In some ways it’s changed a lot, and in others I recognize it completely. We’re in this old, pretty dilapidated building — maybe I shouldn’t use that word — and we joke that we hold it together with bubble gum and rubber bands. Marlow Stern called us “small but mighty” some years ago, and that’s right. We put it together with a huge amount of goodwill. That’s part of the miracle business. But the traditions — the secrecy of the program, the little rituals — are so beloved that when I came back I felt it was important to safeguard all of that.

People imagine we watch movies and go, “OK, we’ll take that one.” It starts out that way, and sometimes distributors and producers want a sense of what we think. I’ve had people say outright, “We’re not sure what we want to do with this movie, but we’d love your input.” Other times we really [want] something, and they say, “We know you like it, but we still want to go next year.”

articles.title: ‘The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Season 5 Trailer Dives Into Taylor Frankie Paul Scandal and Reveals Release Date
articles.summary: Five months after ABC pulled Taylor Frankie Paul’s season of “The Bachelorette,” fans are getting their first on-screen updates about her life. Hulu set a Sept. 10 premiere date for “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” Season 5, which will run for only five episodes compared to previous seasons’ 10.
body: “What do you guys all know about this whole situation?” a producer asks the “Mormon Wives” cast at the start of the trailer. “There’s so much stuff the public doesn’t know,” responds Mayci Neeley in a confessional. “How did she get here?” Miranda Hope says in a scene as the trailer cuts to a shot of Paul sobbing and being hugged by Neeley, Mikayla Matthews and Jessi Draper.

“Why did you get my initials tattooed on your lip? It’s giving obsessed,” Paul says to Mortensen in a FaceTime call. “I am obsessed,” Mortensen replies, showing off the tattoo — which Paul would later cite as a form of harassment when she filed a restraining order against Mortensen.

As the trailer continues, several cast members question their places in each other’s lives as their fame — and infamy — increases. “We all just got pulled in different directions. Where do we stand when we come back together?” Paul says. “We are grown women. This is how we’re acting?” says Neeley. In a confessional, Layla Taylor calls something “definitely unforgivable,” and Draper’s voice is heard saying, “It feels like there are no friendships left in #MomTok.” “The damage is done,” Paul concludes.

articles.title: Jay-Z Documentary Series Sets HBO Release Date
articles.summary: After announcing the documentary series in June, HBO has revealed the release schedule for “Jay-Z in 8,” which will feature the rapper sitting down with music producer and record executive Rick Rubin to discuss the lyrics and ideas for songs across eight episodes.
body: In a trailer for “Jay-Z in 8,” the rapper and Rubin go back and forth about the impact that he had on hip-hop culture and why it’s become such a global force. “The reason why rap is so loved, that feeling of that underdog… That’s why people were listening, that’s why it hit them somewhere,” says Jay.

“Jay-Z in 8,” a Tetragrammaton production, is directed by Rubin and executive produced by Shawn Carter, Daniel Kaluuya and Rubin. Producers include Leila Mattimore and David Rohde. Co-producers are Harlin Lawal and Will Mavronicolas, and director of photography is Bradford Young. HBO executive producers are Nancy Abraham, Lisa Heller and Sara Rodriguez.

The documentary series comes amid a busy year for Jay-Z, who made a grand return to the stage at Philadelphia’s Roots Picnic in late May before staging three historic nights at Yankee Stadium to honor the anniversary milestones of his seminal albums “Reasonable Doubt” and “The Blueprint.” He’s next scheduled to perform shows in London, Paris and Los Angeles, where he’ll take the stage at SoFi Stadium for two nights in late October.

articles.title: De Gaulle: Résistance review – a galloping bromance for Churchill and France’s wartime hero
articles.summary: This biopic of the great Gallic general – which culminates at Bir Hakeim, in advance of a second film – is a fine, quietly amusing romp with a touch of classic 60s war films.
body: Perhaps because it is based on a biography by an Englishman – Julian Jackson’s A Certain Idea of France: The Life of Charles de Gaulle – this very enjoyable and gallopingly eventful biopic, directed by Antonin Baudry, has an element of amused detachment. The first of two parts, it offers a good-humoured, though naturally sympathetic, perspective on France’s great wartime hero, played with martyred and faintly preposterous hauteur by Franco-Armenian actor Simon Abkarian.

Then, we get the high comedy of De Gaulle’s chaotic personal adventures in Africa, finding support for his Free French in Chad and Cameroon, which Churchill admires as audacious if absurd. But Africa is important. An Anglo-Hollywood movie might have seen Britain’s turning point in the war as a matter of dramatising Montgomery’s brilliance at El-Alamein. This French movie instead emphasises the heroism of an outnumbered Free French brigade in the desert at Bir Hakeim under Gen Marie-Pierre Kœnig (Benoît Magimel); inspired by De Gaulle, they hold out against Rommel’s superior forces, giving British forces a chance to retreat and regroup.

articles.title: Rockstar Games breaks silence on Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks
articles.summary: The game developer says the unauthorised footage has caused "heartbreak" for those working on the title.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.
Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.
In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".
The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.
points: The game developer says the unauthorised footage has caused "heartbreak" for those working on the title.

articles.title: Maura Higgins to fill Cilla Black's shoes as host of Blind Date reboot
articles.summary: The Love Island and Traitors US TV personality will host a reboot of the popular dating show.
body: Maura Higgins is set to follow in the footsteps of the late Cilla Black as presenter of Blind Date in a reboot of the popular TV show.
The Irish TV personality rose to fame in 2019 as a finalist on another dating show, Love Island, and more recently appeared on the US version of The Traitors.
The original Blind Date launched on ITV in 1985 and was a staple of Saturday night TV for nearly 20 years, with well-liked Liverpudlian singer and actress Black its host.

It is being revived by Disney+, and on Wednesday the streamer mimicked one of Black's old Blind Date catchphrases in its announcement on Instagram, external: "'Blind Date host, what's your name and where d'ya come from?' It's... Maura Higgins."
points: The Love Island and Traitors US TV personality will host a reboot of the popular dating show.

articles.title: Rupert Grint to return to Harry Potter in Broadway play
articles.summary: Grint, now 38, will play his character as an adult in the Harry Potter spin-off play in New York.
body: Harry Potter star Rupert Grint is to return to the role of Ron Weasley - playing the character as an adult in the spin-off play in New York.
Grint was first cast to play Ron in the original films at the age of 11. Now 38, he will join the cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child on Broadway for four months from next February.

The play catches up with Harry, Ron and Hermione as grown-ups, 19 years after the end of the events in the original books and films - with Ron and Hermione now married and sending their daughter to Hogwarts.
"Dusting off the old robes. New York - see you all in February," Grint wrote on Instagram, external.

articles.title: Shabana Amzi on Her Career, Vulnerability, and “Batwara 1947”
articles.summary: The legendary Hindi actress discusses her life in film and theater, and feeling naked, literally and figuratively, at different moments in her career.
body: Ask any working actor today in the Hindi film industry, and chances are they’ll cite Shabana Azmi as an inspiration. Over a career of 160-plus films that began in 1974, not to mention a record five National Film Awards (India’s equivalent of the Oscars; the most won by any Indian actress), Azmi has demonstrated an extraordinary range that few have approached since.

Though she also worked in commercial Hindi films, Azmi primarily made her mark through the Parallel Cinema movement, a school of filmmaking that prioritized social realism. Without Azmi’s presence, the simmering class tensions of “Ankur,” the marital heartbreak and eventual resilience of “Arth,” or the shocking violence of “Nishant” would lose their main emotional anchor and their long-lasting resonance today. As she built her prolific film career, Azmi also performed onstage, including in “Tumhari, Amrita” (“Yours, Amrita”)—an Indian context adaptation, written by Javed Siddiqui, of A.R. Gurney’s play “ Love Letters ”—a play she performed for 21 years along with co-star Farooque Sheikh.
